fatal_errors: The cited NbMoTaWVTi study does not support a bulk material containing only two BCC solid solutions: SPS produced an FCC TiO precipitate phase.
The cited mechanical properties were explicitly attributed partly to TiO precipitation strengthening, so they cannot substantiate the proposed precipitate-free dual-solid-solution mechanism.
The supplied evidence does not establish a post-SPS grain size below 50 nm.

The falsification experiment does not distinguish grain-boundary strengthening from simple solid-solution strengthening; processing deliberately outside the proposed temperature window and observing coarsening would not falsify the in-window hypothesis.
explanation: The response presents a scientifically recognizable alternative based on mechanical alloying followed by SPS, and its general grain-refinement rationale is plausible. However, it does not reconstruct the target CoCrFeNiTi system, short-duration milling, 900–1000 °C SPS window, or FCC/BCC phase fractions. More importantly, its own evidence contradicts the asserted phase constitution and strengthening mechanism: after SPS, the reported NbMoTaWVTi alloy contains TiO precipitates, and precipitation strengthening contributes to the quoted strengths. The claims of sub-50 nm retained grains, cast-baseline behavior, service instability above 800 °C, and several processing boundaries are not demonstrated by the cited excerpts. A discriminating test should hold composition and phase chemistry constant while varying grain size, then examine strength versus inverse square-root grain size, or compare annealed/coarsened specimens with equivalent solid-solution chemistry; the proposed temperature sweep confounds grain size, phase formation, density, and contamination.
